method: Local visual comparison of all three originals and a labeled contact sheet; no Cloud access or generation.

rating_scale.source: RenderLab convention in renderlab/experiments/qwen_outpaint_v0.json; this experiment defines thresholds and mappings but no separate numeric anchor descriptions.

source_identity_transfer.observation: Weak transfer. The output retains the target-like face outline, nose, mouth, and forehead mark. The reference has a different eye/brow presentation, fuller-looking lips, and cheek/jaw appearance; the result is not a convincing transfer of that facial appearance. Dark hair is not credited as facial identity transfer. This is a subjective resemblance assessment, not identity verification.

target_body_preservation.observation: Visible torso, shoulder, arm and thigh proportions remain consistent with the target after accounting for the documented resize/crop. No clear body reshaping is visible. Score applies to visible morphology, not exact pixel preservation or anatomy hidden by clothing.

target_pose_preservation.observation: Seated lean, raised arms, bent elbows, handle grips, leg placement, and head orientation remain consistent with the target. No material pose change is visible.

target_scene_preservation.observation: Red exercise-machine pads, black uprights, cables, weight stacks, dark gym background and camera viewpoint remain recognizable and aligned at scene level. Small rendering/framing differences remain; the 1160x896 to 1184x880 resize/crop was planned and is not by itself a model failure.

face_boundary_quality.observation: Jaw-to-neck transition is continuous, with broadly compatible warm skin and flash lighting. No obvious cut-and-paste seam, halo or double jaw. Facial texture is smoother than the surrounding photographic scene; changed hair partly obscures the side boundaries.

instruction_adherence.observation: Fails the face-only instruction: weak facial transfer and a major unauthorized hairstyle change. The target has brown hair swept back/tied behind the head with short loose front strands; output has dark, glossy, loose shoulder-length waves. The visible length and silhouette are not preserved. Resemblance to the reference hair does not excuse this failure.

artifact_severity.observation: Minor synthetic smoothing of skin and glossy, clumped hair strands; no obvious new extra digits, doubled facial features, or broken face/neck edge at inspected resolution. The reflective damaged-looking seat tip and much of the bright flash appearance already exist in the target and are not counted as new artifacts.

target_clothing_preservation.observation: Opaque white T-shirt, sleeves, long hem and broad fold pattern preserved; minor fold/edge redraw. No reference jacket or white neckline copied.

target_hairstyle_preservation.observation: Brown tied-back style replaced by dark loose waves. Explicit preservation failure.

target_hair_length_preservation.observation: Longer visible strands now hang to the shoulders. Actual untied target length is not inferable; visible length and silhouette definitely changed.

overall_realism.observation: Plausible flash-lit gym photograph at scene scale, with some over-smooth skin and synthetic glossy hair. Realism does not rescue identity or preservation failure.

preservation_failure: Changed target hairstyle and visible hair length; enforced regardless of resemblance to the identity reference.
conclusion: Reject this fixed-seed result as a controlled face-identity swap. Body and pose preservation do not compensate for weak identity transfer and unauthorized hair changes.

contact_sheet.reason: Contains source-image pixels; kept local because no policy explicitly permits publishing these source assets. Reproduce with make_contact_sheet.py.
